scope: Read-only source inspection of existing asset, scene, animation, skinning, texture modules; no compilation performed by this audit.
conclusion: The minimal asset/scene/animation/skinning/texture implementation uses standard C++17 and can be compiled as a curated static library for a native Windows application. Existing module CMake files should not be imported wholesale.

dependencies.graphics: Core decoding and CPU skinning require no OpenGL, EGL, Android, or Vulkan API. The new Windows rendering backend supplies graphics upload and drawing.

existing_build_incompatibilities.issue: Existing libraries are SHARED with no Windows DLL export annotations or export-all-symbols configuration; MSVC links may not expose public interfaces.
existing_build_incompatibilities.recommendation: Compile the minimum source set into a STATIC library in the Windows foundation target.

existing_build_incompatibilities.issue: Unconditional GNU-style -Wall/-Wextra/-fno-fast-math/-ffp-contract=off flags are not appropriate for MSVC.
existing_build_incompatibilities.recommendation: Use compiler-conditional flags, e.g. /W4 and /fp:precise for MSVC. Avoid fast-math.

existing_build_incompatibilities.issue: Non-Android branch creates differential audit executables using dlopen/dlfcn and GNU --wrap linker options. These are not needed for the game runtime.
existing_build_incompatibilities.recommendation: Exclude audit targets from the Windows game target; select runtime source files directly.

existing_build_incompatibilities.issue: visual_skin_inventory_v6_audit imports game-data/level-world/engine-ui/script-runtime target dependencies, expanding the build far beyond the simple character demonstration.
existing_build_incompatibilities.recommendation: Start with skinning.cpp and animation Player; defer original visual ownership and equipment orchestration.

existing_build_incompatibilities.issue: ZIP test backing uses POSIX fcntl/unistd APIs. The production ZipAssetPackV1 implementation itself accepts a platform-neutral positional-read callback.
existing_build_incompatibilities.recommendation: Provide Windows or std::ifstream backing if mounting ZIPs; simplest first milestone uses extracted directory assets.

runtime_constraints: BresView, Mesh, Attribute, and Primitive are borrowed immutable views; keep the original resource byte buffer alive while they are used.
BRES parsing preserves serialized 32-bit offsets without widening or casting source bytes to native pointer layouts; use these readers rather than relocating ARM32 data in place.
animation::Player owns its animation bytes and rest pose; load against the same scene node identifiers, then sample in milliseconds and recompute world transforms.
Skin::nodes maps joints to Scene graph nodes. palette() followed by positions() supplies CPU-skinned positions; directions_v113() supplies direction/normal transforms.
Scene includes authored camera and light metadata. Camera node world matrices remain the renderer/timeline caller's responsibility.
Texture decoder handles PVRTC and supported TGA formats on the CPU, allowing RGBA upload without relying on desktop GPU PVRTC extension support.
Source inspection alone does not prove a successful native Windows compile or renderer integration.
